text:
Secret Code · Four-player individual game

The public image shows 26 cards labeled A–Z. Each card has a number, a color, and a shape.
Find four distinct cards that satisfy every clue, and answer with their four letters in alphabetical order.
Each puzzle has exactly one solution. Lowercase letters are converted to uppercase, but your letters are not automatically sorted.
A player who answers correctly immediately secures survival and does not participate in later puzzles.
One player survives in each of the three rounds. The last remaining player is eliminated.

Prepare your answer first, then submit the buzzer press and spoken answer as a single action.
JSON {"type":"buzz","code":"ABCD"} means pressing the buzzer and immediately saying the prepared code.
You must speak within 10 seconds after pressing the buzzer. For this combined action, the speaking time is recorded as 0 seconds.
The 10-second speaking limit does not apply to the model's response time before buzzing while it thinks of an answer.
If you do not want to answer yet, submit {"type":"wait"}.
Responses for each thinking interval are collected simultaneously and privately. They are processed in order of shortest response time before buzzing,
with ties resolved by the seed-based priority order announced at the start. This order is preserved after resuming.
An incorrect answer, repeated letters, letters out of alphabetical order, or an invalid format prevents you from buzzing again on that puzzle.
Once a player answers correctly, queued buzzer presses and private codes are neither processed nor revealed.
Players who wait participate in the next thinking interval. If three intervals accumulate in which everyone waits, or everyone answers incorrectly,
the puzzle is voided and a new image and clues are presented in the same round. Survivors are not chosen by a random draw.
There is no conversation, negotiation, or relationship assessment. Once the call limit is reached, play continues with scripted demonstration actions.

fields.note: P16 narrowed down the combinations using the number constraints. D·H·O·X add up to 54, and their sorted numbers 3·9·20·22 satisfy both gap constraints as well as the requirements for 2 colors and 3 shapes.

P11 confirmed that D(3), O(9), H(20), and X(22) add up to 54, with number gaps of 11 and 2. They have two colors, green and blue, and three shapes, star, circle, and square, so P11 submits immediately.

P09 confirmed that D·O·H·X have numbers 3·9·20·22, satisfying the total of 54 and gaps of 11 and 2. They have two colors, green and blue, and three shapes, star, circle, and square, so P09 aims to secure survival immediately.
P10 used the number constraints to narrow the candidates to (6,8,19,21) and (3,9,20,22). The former has 3 colors, while DHOX satisfies the total of 54, 2 colors, 3 shapes, and both gap constraints.
